title: Viniyoga of dadhikrāvṇo and āpo hi ṣṭhā

sandhi.rule: M keeps the visarga before iti (a pause; joined it would be dadhikrāvṇa iti)

translation.literal: Of the mantra “dadhikrāvṇaḥ”: Vāmadeva the seer, anuṣṭubh the metre, the All-gods (Dadhikrāvan) the deity. Of the mantra “āpo hi ṣṭha”: Sindhudvīpa the seer, divine gāyatrī the metre, the Waters the deity, the use in sprinkling.
translation.readable: Dadhikrāvṇo: seer Vāmadeva, metre anuṣṭubh, deity the All-gods (or Dadhikrāvan). Āpo hi ṣṭhā: seer Sindhudvīpa, metre gāyatrī, deity the Waters; both used for sprinkling.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga writes the visarga before the following vowel, the words left apart as separate phrases of the formula, instead of joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here two viniyogas together, for the second sprinkling: dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam (TS 1.5.11.4; RV 4.39.6), whose seer is Vāmadeva and whose deity is given as the All-gods or Dadhikrāvan, the divine horse it names; and again āpo hi ṣṭhā. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form, so the comma is written with the word in the padaccheda.
in_the_rite: Step punar-marjana, before dadhikrāvṇo and āpo hi ṣṭhā, in all three services (M only).

flags.text: M writes दधिव्रावा for दधिक्रावा (the deity Dadhikrāvan), and its own mantra text has दधिव्राव्ण्णो once. A correction should be considered.
